transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, honestly, what scared me enough to make an appointment is something that's been happening at work. I work as a surveillance officer, and lately... well, during the quiet stretches in the surveillance room, I've been hearing voices coming through the monitor speakers. 

They say things to me, like, "You missed it, Ruth," or "People are going to get hurt because of you." But the thing is, every channel on my board is completely muted. And no one else in the room hears anything at all. It's just me hearing it. So... I figured I needed to talk to a doctor about it.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
It's been going on for about four months now. It started right around the time I was moved into the lead casino surveillance role.
Do you hear these voices when you are away from work?
No, I don't. It's... it's just at work. When I'm home, or out running errands, it's quiet. I don't hear them anywhere else, just when I'm sitting in that surveillance room.
When you hear them, do they sound like real voices coming from the monitor speakers, or do they feel like thoughts inside your own mind?

They sound completely real. It's not like a thought in my head at all. It sounds exactly like someone is speaking right through the monitor speakers. I hear it out loud, clear as day, telling me, "You missed it, Ruth," or that people are going to get hurt. That's what makes it so terrifying... it sounds like a real person talking to me, but I know every channel is muted and none of the other officers hear it.
Before these voices began, had you started using any recreational drugs, or increased your use of them?
No, I don't use any drugs. I never have. I don't even really drink, maybe just a glass of wine on a holiday or something. So, no, nothing like that.
Since the voices began, have you developed any strong beliefs that other people might consider unusual or untrue?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I know the voices aren't really there, even though they sound like it. But other than that, no, I haven't started believing anything strange or unusual. I just go to work, deal with the monitors, and come home. There's nothing else going on in my head like that.
Have the voices interfered with your ability to do your job?

Yes, they definitely have. I've already made some mistakes on my shift paperwork because I'm so distracted by them. And it's not just work... I've had to step back from my friends and the things I usually do because I just can't keep up the way I used to. When I get home, I mostly just get through the bare minimum. I don't really cook anymore, I haven't had anyone over, and I've completely stopped taking care of any projects around the house. It's just too much.
Have you noticed your thoughts or speech becoming disorganized or difficult for others to follow?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I think I'm speaking just fine, and no one has mentioned having a hard time understanding me. My thoughts are definitely crowded with the voices and the sadness, but they aren't jumbled up or anything. I can still communicate clearly.
Since the voices began, have you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yes. Most days, it's just... there. It feels like this heavy, gray mood settles over me before I even get out of bed. And it stays with me. I'll be sitting in my car before my shift starts, and I'll just start tearing up over nothing. Just seeing the casino lights can make me cry. It's pretty much every day.
Did the depressed mood begin before the voices started, or did the voices begin before you became depressed?

The depressed mood definitely started first. I started feeling really hopeless and, I don't know, just guilty all the time after they changed the surveillance lead at work. It was only after that stretch of feeling so low that I started hearing the voices through the equipment. I'd never heard those kinds of accusations before, or felt so sure that I was a danger to everyone around me. So yeah, the voices and those beliefs... they only started after I was already in this really low period. They just seem to be part of it now.
Have there been any times since the voices began when you felt no longer depressed but the voices continued?

No, not really. It's all just been... happening together. Like I was saying before, before this whole stretch of feeling so hopeless and guilty after the surveillance lead changed, I had never heard those accusations through the equipment. And I'd never felt so certain that I was dangerous to everyone. The voices and those beliefs... they only seem to be part of this same low period. There hasn't been a time where the sadness went away but the voices stayed. It's all just one big, heavy thing.
